task: Module 3 commerce requirements and roadmap closure

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The change affects the canonical roadmap authority rather than commerce runtime. High-risk review is deliberately retained because accepted merchant and customer obligations, package entitlements, and launch priority could be distorted by a misleading roadmap edit. Assurance covers exact two-file scope, truth-status preservation, source-bound audit traceability, valid canonical guard selection and regression evidence. It explicitly does not certify live Szamlazz.hu, Billingo, refunds, shipping, payment gateways, tax behavior, provider credentials, production schema, or end-to-end commerce functionality.

acceptanceCriteria: The only business-content changes are the Module 3 audit document and the existing canonical living-roadmap JSON; the old closed Development Transaction remains preserved on main and is replaced only by this new scoped local planning transaction.

The audit contains accepted functional obligations 3.1 through 3.12, a per-capability implementation/proof discrepancy crosswalk, precise partial or unproven status, and explicit source-inspection limitations.

The existing roadmap items retain their identity and maturity status; Billingo becomes a launch obligation alongside Szamlazz.hu in INVOICE-FOUNDATION while unrelated future invoice and ERP adapters remain post-launch.

Every financial, tax, provider and entitlement claim is a scope or verification requirement, never a statement that production behavior has passed. Alap retains essential safe commerce, invoicing and recovery; Pro only adds advanced workflow.

The exact two-file change passes the repository canonical preflight, plan-before-code, edit-time, replay, roadmap/quality regression, risk, CI, Completion Truth and lifecycle gates with evidence tied to the actual branch and source commit.
invariants: No runtime, database, payment, invoice, fulfillment, email, secret, production environment or customer state is changed by this docs-and-roadmap transaction.
No accepted PO business decision is reopened or silently weakened, especially Billingo and Szamlazz.hu Alap+Pro launch scope and guest, refund, fiscal and merchant operations.
Roadmap statuses and closed-loop proof remain unchanged: documentation of a launch requirement is never implementation completion evidence.
The canonical roadmap and the new audit are the only material deliverables; do not create duplicate capability engines, parallel roadmap authorities or independently invented gates.
The Development Transaction base remains the actual main HEAD at the time of planning and requires reconciliation if the target main HEAD advances before execution.
forbiddenStates: Billingo remains described as post-launch-only while the PO has accepted it for initial launch.
Any roadmap capability is promoted to DONE because its requirement was documented.
A cosmetic green CI result replaces exact base identity, Completion Truth, lifecycle closure or real implementation proof.
The old closed DEV-CORE-1186 transaction is repurposed by merely patching its base SHA.
Implementation files, provider credentials or production schemas are changed within this documentation-only release.

failureModes: Stale main base or reused closed plan yields CI_TRANSACTION_BASE_MISMATCH before any meaningful build or acceptance evidence.
Billingo wording remains post-launch or new invoice requirement accidentally drops the previously accepted merchant-bound legal lifecycle.
A document says a feature is implemented or DONE merely because an adapter or route exists, creating a false completion claim.
A roadmap edit changes item identifiers, statuses or other phases unexpectedly, corrupting canonical roadmap authority.
Cross-package marketing or refund workflow language accidentally gates basic safe Alap merchant operations behind Pro.
Unscoped additions to implementation or provider systems bypass the expected two-file change and require new authorities/proofs.
Reference, knowledge, failure-selection or quality regression breaks even though the JSON syntax is valid.
edgeCases: Only the audit document changes but the invoice roadmap still says Billingo is post-launch.
A matching but stale main SHA has been superseded by another merge before the new PR is opened.
An accepted invoice connector is described as included in Alap while its provider subscription fee is incorrectly promised free.
New rows correctly describe defects but are erroneously marked proved by the source-only inspection.
The audit reports an unconfirmed admin-order endpoint as definitely absent rather than unproven in the scoped review.
The diff adds audit text but removes a previously accepted product requirement from a roadmap item.
An unrelated documentation diff creeps into the release and bypasses planned-file scope.

alternatives.summary: Use the generated high-risk Development Transaction to replay the previously reviewed two-file changes against exact main with an independent truthful verification path.
alternatives.reason: Preserves canonical roadmap authority and the completed commercial requirement audit while making transaction identity and evidence verifiable before merge.

alternatives.summary: Patch only the old closed DEV-CORE-1186 development transaction base and rerun the existing failed CI.
alternatives.reason: The closed transaction governs different files and proof. Updating its SHA would falsify task identity and conceal missing planning authorization.

alternatives.summary: Merge the earlier draft documentation PR through a documentation-only CI skip or mark the change verified without a new Development Transaction.
alternatives.reason: The roadmap JSON is an authoritative quality-system input, so bypassing transaction and completion gates would weaken mandatory proof semantics.

specialistReviews.finding: The generated Atlas route assigns DOMAIN-QUALITY and quality-knowledge-system to the existing roadmap file while treating the new audit Markdown as a neutral unclassified document.
specialistReviews.resolution: Restrict material implementation to the exact roadmap JSON and audit Markdown; retain existing roadmap IDs and reuse the existing canonical planning, guard and truth systems.

specialistReviews.finding: The earlier PR 1235 is based on main 615700e but still carries the unrelated closed DEV-CORE-1186 plan. The CI_TRANSACTION_BASE_MISMATCH is a real transaction admission failure, not a harmless docs warning.
specialistReviews.resolution: Construct a fresh scoped plan before replaying any content; explicitly block merging or claiming CI pass until exact-base preflight, CI, Truth and lifecycle proofs succeed.

specialistReviews.finding: The accepted change concerns documented merchant fiscal/stock/payment obligations; its audit describes incomplete tenant-scoped credentials, card refunds, guest retries and invoice lifecycle without treating source presence as live truth.
specialistReviews.resolution: Bind testable claims to the bounded documentation scope, preserve all existing roadmap statuses and explicitly leave live provider, tenant and financial proof PARTIAL until future implementation cycles.

specialistReviews.finding: The generated guard activated 49 preventive failure records and flagged knowledge-infrastructure change requiring full replay; these are applicable protections, not evidence of 49 fresh failures.
specialistReviews.resolution: Read the prevention instructions before implementation and run preflight, edit-time guard and incremental replay after the coherent two-file edit batch; report any new failure without scope expansion.

challenge.scenario: A documentation PR starts CI with a closed plan belonging to a previously completed Office readiness task.
challenge.finding: The plan base, task and planned file scope do not match the actual PR; safety gates must prevent accidental admission.
challenge.resolution: Generate a new exact-main module 3 Development Transaction before changes and demand independent PASS from canonical Plan Before Code.

challenge.scenario: The audit calls Billingo a launch requirement but the roadmap retains Billingo in the postlaunch adapter program.
challenge.finding: Conflicting authorities would mislead release prioritization and break accepted PO obligations.
challenge.resolution: Update INVOICE-FOUNDATION and explicitly distinguish other future provider adapters in POSTLAUNCH-ADAPTER-ECOSYSTEM; inspect final two-file diff.

challenge.scenario: A source-only audit assumes that seeing an invoice route proves legal invoice corrections and merchant-scoped credentials in production.
challenge.finding: Adapter presence cannot prove provider behavior, tenant isolation, fiscal correctness or customer flow closure.
challenge.resolution: Keep PARTIAL and UNPROVEN findings with source inspection limitations; forbid roadmap DONE promotion until dedicated end-to-end evidence.

challenge.scenario: A well-intentioned docs edit changes unrelated statuses, IDs or dependencies in the canonical roadmap.
challenge.finding: Schema-valid JSON may still produce authority drift or incorrectly reprioritize major capabilities.
challenge.resolution: Compare selected entry identities and statuses against the exact main base and verify the PR diff contains only approved two-file semantic changes.

challenge.scenario: The Alap package unintentionally loses standard refund, error recovery or invoice integrations when advanced Pro workflow is specified.
challenge.finding: The commercial split would violate accepted baseline safety and launch packaging decisions.
challenge.resolution: Preserve essential financial safety and both invoices in Alap+Pro, assigning only nonessential configurable depth and analytics to Pro.

challenge.scenario: Development proceeds even though the known-failure selection returns baseline-only and many template-related records.
challenge.finding: A large guard inventory could be misconstrued as 49 live defects or tempt implementers to disable guard selection.
challenge.resolution: Confirm DOMAIN-QUALITY authority and knowledge-infrastructure full replay, retain generated failure inventory and do not claim new defects without evidence.

challenge.scenario: A green guard or deploy preview is offered as proof that Billingo, card refund and chargeback are implemented.
challenge.finding: Guard PASS only attests to the planned documentation transaction, not runtime/provider acceptance.
challenge.resolution: Limit this transaction completion claim to roadmap/audit documentation. Track actual commerce closure separately through dependency and integration evidence.

challenge.scenario: Another PR advances main before this plan reaches the repository and the earlier base identity becomes stale.
challenge.finding: The exact target base SHA is no longer the release base, making existing evidence and transaction identity stale.
challenge.resolution: Stop and regenerate or explicitly reconcile a fresh transaction on the new main; never simply overwrite the base SHA in a closed plan.

proofPlan: Run canonical shoperation-plan-before-code.mjs --check locally before replaying the two changed content files and inspect structured issues rather than ignoring warnings.
Check exact-main git identity and the two-file diff; require valid JSON, stable roadmap item IDs and statuses, accepted Billingo launch placement and no unrelated authority changes.
Run scripts/shoperation-edit-time-guard.mjs --check, scripts/shoperation-knowledge-preflight.mjs and scripts/shoperation-incremental-replay.mjs --check after the coherent edit batch.
Execute relevant capability-roadmap and quality-system regression tests plus the repository release-risk checker and full required CI; do not infer passing results in advance.

Verify the new Pull Request CI is green for its exact head and base, and that Completion Truth and Lifecycle Close to Learn have valid noncircular evidence before claiming this documentation transaction DONE.
Retain the remaining Module 3 runtime and provider gaps as PARTIAL or UNPROVEN in the roadmap and audit; do not claim legal, merchant, payment or invoicing certification from documentation checks.

requirements.requirement: The module 3 change is limited to the audit Markdown and existing canonical living-roadmap JSON with an exact scoped Development Transaction; no application, migration or secret changes are admitted.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: An unrelated runtime or governance file cannot be silently accepted as an in-scope edit.

requirements.requirement: The canonical roadmap preserves existing identities and statuses while recording the accepted 3.1-3.12 business obligations, both launch invoice adapters and Alap versus Pro entitlement boundaries.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A roadmap item must not be marked done solely because this documentation audit states an accepted launch requirement.

requirements.requirement: The audit remains explicitly source-bounded and records implementation gaps as partial or unproven, with no provider certification or false end-to-end completion claims.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Source file existence alone must never be reported as verified merchant/provider runtime closure.

notes: Prepared for independent canonical Plan Before Code verification against main SHA 615700e. This is the bounded documentation transaction only; no commerce runtime acceptance or product completion implied. SpecialistReviews record role-based source-review analyses, not independent human attestations. On a changed main base, regenerate the transaction before execution. Completion Truth, required CI and lifecycle remain outstanding.
